properties.description:
PlanetRisk is a U.S. defense contractor that developed surveillance capabilities using commercially collected mobile location and advertising data. In 2015, iMapData, a data visualization and analysis company, merged with PlanetRisk, and the newly formed company took the PlanetRisk name.

In 2016, the company developed Locomotive, a phone tracking platform that combined location data purchased from commercial brokers with tools for mapping and analyzing the movements of mobile devices. The system could identify where devices traveled and establish patterns of movement. 

PlanetRisk initially demonstrated Locomotive using data from Syria, where it obtained information on roughly 168,000 mobile devices in Aleppo and was able to observe the movement of refugees fleeing the country's civil war. 

The company obtained the underlying location data from UberMedia, which offered a global feed containing data on mobile devices collected through the digital advertising ecosystem. Pentagon research organizations provided approximately $600,000 to develop the initial Locomotive demonstration, and government officials subsequently pushed PlanetRisk to keep the capability quiet. 

Locomotive was later taken to Aelius Exploitation Technologies, where it was renamed VISR (Virtual Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance) and developed for use by the U.S. intelligence community.

PlanetRisk Federal Services was acquired by Culmen International in 2018. Separately, Everbridge acquired assets of the original PlanetRisk, Inc. that same year for $2 million.

properties.description:
Proctorio is an Arizona-based remote proctoring company whose software is used by universities to monitor students during online exams. Marketed as an "academic integrity" tool, the platform functions as an invasive surveillance system installed directly on students' personal computers.

Once enabled, Proctorio harvests a sweeping set of personal data and biometric signals from test-takers in their own homes, including face images and webcam video of the student, driver's license or other ID information, network and device details, audio from the student's microphone and a scan of the room, algorithmic tracking of "abnormal" eye movements, head movements, and other body language, all of which is then flagged for instructors to review as potentially "suspicious" behavior.

properties.providing to: United States; Australia; Canada; United Kingdom
properties.funders: Eastside Partners
properties.description:
ProctorU is an online proctoring service used by universities and certification bodies to monitor students during remote exams, combining live human proctors with AI-driven surveillance to "detect potential cheating in real time," according to its marketing materials. 

Its monitoring capabilities typically include webcam and microphone access that records the student's face, eye movements, and ambient audio throughout the exam, along with screen recording and screen sharing that gives proctors full visibility into everything displayed on the test-taker's device. 

Before an exam begins, students are typically required to complete ID verification and room scans, showing photo identification and panning their camera around the room. During the session, behavioral AI analysis flags "suspicious" actions such as looking away from the screen, background noise, multiple faces, or unusual keystroke patterns, while browser and network lockdown features restrict tabs, copy-paste, and external connections.

Researchers have documented that ProctorU frequently produces false positives, and its facial detection software has been shown to struggle with recognizing people of color, often forcing them to sit under harsh lighting just to be verified. A 2020 breach that leaked hundreds of thousands of user records created massive concerns about how it handles biometric and ID data.

properties.name: Qosmos
properties.description:
Qosmos was a French technology company that developed Deep Packet Inspection (DPI) software. It has faced significant scrutiny for reportedly supplying surveillance tools to oppressive regimes, including Bashar al-Assad's government in Syria, confirmed by several investigations. The company's software is capable of monitoring internet traffic, which can be used to track dissidents and suppress opposition.

In 2012, French authorities opened a judicial investigation into Qosmos for its potential complicity in crimes against humanity. Advocacy groups and human rights organizations have criticized Qosmos for failing to ensure its technology was not misused.

In 2016, it was acquired by Swedish company ENEA.

properties.description:
Recorded Future is a cyber intelligence company founded by Swedish entrepreneur Christopher Ahlberg and headquartered in Somerville, Massachusetts. The company specializes in analyzing vast datasets, both public and private, to provide intelligence. It is a major provider to U.S. defense, intelligence, and law enforcement agencies, including the NSA’s Cyber Command, and the Secret Service, securing multi-million-dollar federal contracts over the years. Israel's National Cyber Security Authority is also a user of the company's tools.

Former NSA officer Lori Stroud joined Recorded Future in 2019. Before this role, Stroud was involved in the UAE's cyber-offensive Project Raven, conducted with the National Electronic Security Authority (NESA) and DarkMatter, and which used spyware to target journalists and human rights defenders in the UAE and Saudi Arabia.

In September 2024, Recorded Future was acquired by Mastercard for $2.65 billion.

Amazon Rekognition is a facial recognition and image analysis service that uses deep learning to identify objects, people, and activities in images and videos. properties.name: ResidentBat
properties.description:
ResidentBat is an Android spyware operation attributed with high confidence to the Belarusian KGB that transforms victims' smartphones into surveillance devices. According to forensic research by Reporters Without Borders, it has been active since at least March 2021. The spyware specifically targets individuals of interest to the Belarusian security services, including Belarus-based journalists who have been interrogated by the KGB.

Its capabilities include monitoring messaging apps (Telegram, Signal, WhatsApp, Viber) through screen capture, intercepting text messages and calls, accessing device storage, camera and microphone, capturing browser data and clipboard content, and enabling remote device wiping.

properties.name: Respondus
properties.description:
Respondus is a developer of surveillance software that monitors students' laptops, tablets, and phones during exams, tracking eye movements, keystrokes, screen activity, web searches, and physical location. Through its LockDown Browser and Respondus Monitor products, the company enables the webcam and microphone to record video and audio of the test-taker's body and room, while algorithms flag "suspicious" behavior for an instructor to review later, which students described as feeling "dystopian."

properties.description:
Ring, acquired by Amazon in 2018 for approximately $1 billion, is a smart doorbell and security camera company that has become central to a major surveillance controversy due to its extensive partnerships with police departments across the United States. These partnerships have allowed law enforcement to request doorbell and security camera footage directly from Ring users, often without requiring a warrant. 

Ring shut down its direct police request feature in January 2024. However, the company reversed course in July 2025 by partnering with Axon to reintroduce police access to user footage through Axon's digital evidence management system.

In October 2025, Ring announced a partnership with Flock, a network of AI cameras used by law enforcement, enabling agencies to request Ring users to share surveillance footage.

A few months later, in February 2026, Ring cancelled its partnership with Flock after major backlash and campaigns by various advocacy groups.

In June 2026, Amazon was hit with a class action lawsuit filed in Seattle, alleging that Ring's "Familiar Faces" feature stores facial-recognition data of passersby without their consent.

properties.description:
Ripple Labs is a San Francisco-based cryptocurrency and fintech company behind the XRP digital payment protocol. Since 2025, the company has also become a significant private funder of police surveillance infrastructure in San Francisco, directly hosting a major law enforcement surveillance facility within its own corporate offices.

Ripple Labs and a nonprofit backed by its billionaire co-founder Chris Larsen offered a combined $9.4 million donation to the San Francisco Police Department (SFPD) to fund the relocation and expansion of the department's Real-Time Investigation Center (R-TIC), a surveillance hub that aggregates live feeds from cameras, drones, and license plate readers across the city. The SFPD accepted the gift in June 2025.

R-TIC, now housed within Ripple's offices, gives SFPD investigators access to over 400 license plate reader (LPR) cameras deployed across San Francisco, more than 60 drones for aerial surveillance, and real-time monitoring and investigative tools.

Robotec Colombia is a Colombian technology company that served as an intermediary and distributor for Italian spyware vendor Hacking Team in Latin America. Leaked Hacking Team documents show that Robotec brokered sales of Hacking Team's Remote Control System (RCS/Galileo) to government agencies in Colombia, Ecuador, and Panama. properties.name: Root Networks
properties.description:
Root Networks (RN) is an Israeli company that developed systems capable of infiltrating local area networks (LANs) and intercepting communications without requiring cooperation from telecom operators. This capability enables intelligence services to conduct long-term surveillance and execute Man-in-the-Middle attacks to access encrypted communications. Captured data is redirected via VPN tunnels for detailed analysis.

RN's technology exploits vulnerabilities in router firmware to gain remote access. By mapping and infiltrating vulnerable routers, the company establishes its own interception network, independent of traditional operators. This network allows RN to monitor target devices, such as smartphones and computers, and deploy spyware for further surveillance.

Root Networks was founded by Avi Yarim, a former Rayzone Group specialist, and was led by CTO Shahar Mor, an ex-cybersecurity researcher at Verint. The company shares investors with Rayzone Group, including prominent figures like Yohai Ben-Zakai, a former deputy commander of Unit 8200, and businessman Eran Reshef.

properties.description:
S2T Unlocking Cyberspace provides AI-powered surveillance technologies. The firm bills itself as an open-source intelligence (OSINT) company, but a confidential brochure, found by Forbidden Stories in a trove of over 500,000 leaked Colombian military documents, reveals capabilities that go far beyond typical OSINT. These include an automated phishing tool to remotely install malware, access to massive advertising databases for tracking targets, automated influence operations using fake social media accounts, facial recognition, and location tracking that claims to "reach nearly every smartphone user".

S2T was founded in 2002 by entrepreneur Ori Sasson, with current or former offices in Singapore, Sri Lanka, the UK, and Israel. The company claims to have dozens of clients across five continents and employs people from intelligence agencies in the UK, the US, Russia, and Israel, as well as local law enforcement in the Middle East, South and Central America, and Asia. 

Forbidden Stories identified clients in Singapore and Israel, and possible customers in Bangladesh, Turkey, Sri Lanka, India, and Malaysia. The brochure also references demos apparently given in 2020, including to the Indian Navy. An S2T subsidiary appears to have made a shipment to Bangladesh's Directorate General of Forces Intelligence (DGFI) in late 2021 or early 2022.

Forbidden Stories also identified an Israel-based company, KS Process and Software Ltd., as a possible reseller of S2T's technology. KS Process shares at least one address and phone number with S2T. On its website, the company boasts of social-engineering tactics used to trick targets into sharing personal information and appears to have worked on behalf of a "Turkish political party," using social media avatars to infiltrate closed groups and collect intelligence on opponents.

properties.providing to: Algeria; Afghanistan; Azerbaijan; Egypt; Eritrea; Jordan; Kuwait; Pakistan; Qatar; Russia; Sudan; Thailand; Turkey; United Arab Emirates; Uzbekistan; Syria; Bahrain; Belarus
properties.description:
Sandvine was founded in 2001 in Waterloo, Ontario, by a team of ~30 people from PixStream (a Cisco acquisition).

The company developed deep packet inspection (DPI) technology for network traffic management, which is also used for censorship and surveillance purposes. In 2017, San Francisco-based private equity firm Francisco Partners acquired Sandvine and merged it with its U.S.-based holding Procera Networks in a deal valued at approximately $562 million. Procera had separately developed DPI technology that was used for surveillance and censorship in countries with authoritarian regimes.

Following the merger, Sandvine struck deals with several governments, including in Belarus, Egypt, Eritrea, the United Arab Emirates, and Uzbekistan. By 2023, Egypt alone accounted for $26 million in annual sales, roughly 13% of the company's total revenue. That same year, researchers at Citizen Lab discovered Sandvine's technology had been used in attempts to inject spyware into the iPhone of Ahmed Eltantawy, an Egyptian politician planning to challenge President El-Sisi.

In February 2024, the U.S. Commerce Department added Sandvine to its Entity List for providing Egypt with "mass web-monitoring and censorship" technology used to block news and target political actors and human rights activists. The blacklisting effectively banned Sandvine from obtaining U.S. technology, and major firms including Microsoft, Zoom, and Intel cut ties with the company. Francisco Partners exited its ownership in August 2024

The DOC removed Sandvine from the Entity List in October, 2024, after the company promised to "undergo transformative changes."

The company has since rebranded to AppLogic Networks.

SecurCube, an Italian digital forensics company founded in 2012 by Nicola Chemello and Massimo Bastianon, provides mobile phone and geolocation forensics tools. These include BTS Tracker, a hardware and software solution that collects and maps data on GSM, UMTS, and LTE cell tower coverage, providing a statistical analysis of real signal coverage, PhoneLog, a tool designed to analyze and validate call detail records (CDRs) and mobile device extractions, and Downloader, software for extracting IMAP email accounts and Google location history. The company has Cellebrite-certified engineers.

In 2022, the company was acquired by A+GROUP, the parent company of Italian lawful interception specialist Area, led by Andrea Franco Formenti. Recently, SecurCube has been expanding its reach in the UAE, with its tools being added to the catalogue of Scientific Analytical Tools, an Emirati intelligence equipment reseller.

properties.description:
Secure Planet is a biometric technology company that develops facial recognition and identity intelligence systems for defense, intelligence, and law enforcement agencies. The company's products include FABIS Mobile, which performs facial recognition on handheld devices and can match against galleries without a network connection; BioCore, which combines facial, fingerprint, tattoos or scars, license plate recognition and video analytics; and long range facial recognition systems capable of identifying people from distances of up to 300 meters.

Secure Planet also runs TacID Guard Dog, a real-time biometric capture, screening, and alerting system designed for border control and defense teams. The system incorporated facial recognition algorithms from Rank One Computing.

The company has received U.S. military funding, including a $2.85 million 2024 award for advanced tactical facial recognition at a distance.

properties.description:
Securly is a student monitoring platform. It provides schools with tools to monitor and manage student activity both online and offline. Its features include using AI to analyze student online activity, a cloud-based web filtering system that blocks content, and a tracker that identifies "potential risks." Securly's On-Call team actively monitors alerts and escalates cases to appropriate authorities, including the police. According to multiple reports and a class action lawsuit led by parents, Securly illegally collected their children’s private data without their knowledge and sold it to third parties.

In March 2021, Golden Gate Capital, a private equity firm, acquired Securly from its shareholders, including co-founder Vinay Mahadik, Defy Partners, and Owl Ventures. Following the acquisition, Securly continued to operate under the leadership of co-founder and CEO Bharath Madhusudan, and most recently Tammy Wincup.

properties.name: Securus Technologies
properties.funders: Platinum Equity; ABRY Partners
properties.also known as: TZ Holdings Inc. (former name, 1986–2009); Aventiv Technologies (parent)
properties.description:
Securus Technologies was founded in 1986 as TZ Holdings, Inc. in Dallas, Texas. In April 2009, the company changed its name to Securus Technologies, Inc and began operating as part of Aventiv Technologies, which is owned by Platinum Equity.

The company develops communications, monitoring, and investigative technologies for prisons, jails, probation agencies, and law enforcement.

Securus's products records and monitors both voice and video calls, layers on AI call analytics and voice biometrics, and runs investigative platforms that flag suspicious communications and map relationships between people. Its portfolio also spans digital forensics, GPS ankle monitors, and jail management software. 

In 2015, documents leaked to The Intercept revealed that a hacker had obtained records of more than 70 million prisoner phone calls from Securus' systems, including at least 14,000 recorded conversations between incarcerated people and their attorneys.

In 2018, Securus provided a location tracking service that allowed law enforcement customers to obtain real-time cellphone location data with insufficient verification of court authorization.

Securus acquired DirectHit Systems (data analytics), Satellite Tracking of People (STOP) for GPS tracking, and JLG Technologies (voice biometrics and analytics).

properties.providing to: Azerbaijan; Chad; Comoros; Côte d'Ivoire; Cyprus; Congo; Gabon; Gambia; Guinea-Bissau; Ireland; Libya; Madagascar; Mozambique; Rwanda; Senegal; Somalia; Zimbabwe; El Salvador; Lithuania
properties.subsidiaries: Locosem, Semlex Bissau SA, Semlex Ivory Coast, Semlex Guinea-Bissau
properties.description:
Semlex develops and operates biometric identification and border management systems for governments. Its products include biometric passports, digital identity systems, and biometric border control infrastructure. In The Gambia, Semlex supplied a border management system that scans identity documents and feeds travellers’ biographic and biometric information into national databases and the International Organization for Migration’s MIDAS system. The company has also supplied biometric border control and identification systems in countries including Mozambique, Rwanda and Gabon.

Investigations by the Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project (OCCRP) found evidence of alleged bribes, kickbacks and payments to politically connected intermediaries in several African countries. In Madagascar, for example, OCCRP reported that Semlex paid a former senior government official more than €120,000 in unexplained payments while he was involved in securing government business for the company. OCCRP also reported evidence of Semlex's use of politically connected intermediaries in Chad and The Gambia.

In the Democratic Republic of Congo, the allegations concern Semlex's contract to produce biometric passports. Belgian prosecutors investigated the arrangement after reports that $60 from each $185 passport payment was channelled to a Dubai based company linked to an associate of former President Joseph Kabila. In September 2026, a Brussels court referred Semlex and 13 other defendants to the Belgian criminal court on allegations including corruption of foreign public officials, money laundering and tax fraud.

properties.name: Semptian
properties.description:
Semptian, a Chinese company, manufactures surveillance tools used by authoritarian governments across the Middle East and North Africa. These tools, including the Aegis system, Owlet, Falcon, and HawkEye, enable extensive monitoring of citizens' digital activities and communications. Its technologies are also capable of intercepting emails, such as Gmail (through a tool called Gmail Retriever), and analyzing vast amounts of data for surveillance purposes. They also develop GSM geo-location tools and the POMS (Public Opinion Monitoring System) platform for social media monitoring. 

Semptian collaborates with American companies like IBM and Xilinx to enhance its surveillance capabilities, despite concerns over human rights abuses in the regions where its technology is deployed. The company's devices intercept phone calls, texts, and internet usage.

Headquartered in Shenzhen, the company is led by its founder Chen Longsen, also known as George Chen, who previously served as the director of the local branch of the American cryptography and computer security company SafeNet.

properties.name: SenAI
properties.funders: 1948 Ventures; 10D; FS Ventures
properties.description:
SenAI is an Israeli startup building what it calls Online Video Intelligence (OVINT). Its primary clients are governments and intelligence agencies. Its platform runs multimodal AI, combining computer vision, audio analysis, language processing, and geospatial inference across videos on social media to assess what is happening on the ground. From these scattered clips, the system identifies what appears in a video, pinpoints where it was filmed, and links it to other footage posted nearby or at similar times, helping authorities see what's happening, and where, in real time.

SenAI says it has been testing the technology in partnership with governments across Europe, Asia, and the Middle East.

properties.name: SenseNets
properties.description:
SenseNets, a Chinese company that provides facial recognition software and video-based crowd analysis, is heavily involved in surveillance activities, particularly in East Turkistan (renamed Xinjiang by China.) The company operates a massive database that has been used to monitor the Uyghur population.

In 2019, Victor Gevers, a Dutch security researcher, discovered that SenseNets had left a database exposed online without authentication. This database contained sensitive personal information on over 2.5 million individuals, including names, ID card details, home addresses, photos, and GPS tracking data. The system actively recorded millions of GPS coordinates daily, tracking individuals' movements across locations such as mosques, hotels, police stations, and restaurants. The database also included information on public camera locations, suggesting integration with government surveillance infrastructure.

SenseNets is part of China's Skynet Project, a national mass surveillance system. The company also has connections to prominent AI researchers and institutions, such as the Chinese University of Hong Kong, as well as other major Chinese surveillance firms like SenseTime and Hikvision.

properties.description:
Serco is a government services company that operates the UK Ministry of Justice's electronic monitoring service in England and Wales. Since May 2024, it has been responsible for processing monitoring orders, fitting and removing electronic monitoring devices, and monitoring people for the duration of their orders. Its systems use GPS and radio frequency technology to track people’s location and flag breaches of their conditions.

Jacobin reported in April 2024 on the experience of a person subject to the device, describing the system as continuous surveillance and noting that the Home Office had expanded the use of surveillance technology against migrants since 2021.

In evidence to the House of Commons Justice Committee on 19 May 2026, Serco's managing director said that approximately 29,000 people were being monitored at the end of April 2026, an increase of around 8,000 since Serco took over the contract. He also said that approximately 4,500 immigration cases were being monitored, mostly using GPS tags.

In February 2024, the UK Information Commissioner’s Office ordered Serco Leisure to stop using facial recognition and fingerprint technology to monitor staff attendance at 38 leisure centers after finding that the biometric data of more than 2,000 employees had been unlawfully processed.

properties.name: Serpro
properties.description:
Serpro (Serviço Federal de Processamento de Dados) is a Brazilian state owned technology company that provides digital infrastructure and data services to the federal government. Its surveillance and identification capabilities include facial and fingerprint biometrics, identity verification, and automated matching against government databases. Its AIBIO biometric platform supports face, fingerprint, voice, document, and biographical-data validation and has been described by Serpro as being built on databases containing approximately 220 million facial images and 2 billion fingerprints. The company also offers one-to-many facial recognition, which can compare an unidentified face against a government database to determine a person's identity. Serpro's biometric systems have been used for airport passenger identification and other government identity programs, while its Datavalid service allows public and private organizations to verify facial and fingerprint biometrics against official federal databases.

In 2020, documents obtained by The Intercept Brasil showed that Brazil's intelligence agency, Abin, sought access through Serpro to photographs and other information from the CNH database, which contained data on roughly one third of Brazil's population at the time. The request would have given intelligence personnel access to a database containing drivers' photographs and other identifying information.

Sistemas Integrales Computarizados, S.A. de C.V. (SICSA) is a Mexican technology company that has supplied surveillance and biometric systems to government agencies. In 2018, Veracruz's Secretaría de Seguridad Pública contracted SICSA for a system for analyzing emotional reactions in voice and a video analysis system with facial recognition capabilities.

The company has also participated in government procurement for video-surveillance infrastructure. In a 2013 Mexico City audit, Sistemas Integrales Computarizados was among the companies that submitted bids for the acquisition and installation of video-surveillance cameras for three neighborhoods in the Miguel Hidalgo borough.

properties.kinds: Social Media Monitoring; AI-Powered; Data Broker
properties.funders: Techstars; Bossa Invest; Sinai Capital Partners; Right Side Capital; Contour Venture Partners; MS&AD Ventures; Colle Capital Partners; NXT Ventures; Alpine Meridian; Runway Venture Partners; Caerus Investment Partners
properties.description:
Skopenow is a surveillance and investigative tool that aggregates publicly available data from social media platforms, websites, and other online sources to create detailed profiles of individuals. It is designed to assist law enforcement, private investigators, and corporate security teams in identifying, tracking, and analyzing individuals' online activities. The platform automates the process of collecting and organizing information, such as social media posts, photos, connections, and public records, with the primary purpose of profiling and monitoring targets. Its AI capabilities allow it to identify patterns, connections, and relationships between individuals, as well as extract relevant insights from unstructured data like images, videos, and text. 

Skopenow is commonly used by police departments.

properties.description:
Skydio, founded in 2014, is a U.S. drone manufacturer and developer of autonomous flight technology. The company develops and distributes in AI-powered drones equipped with autonomous capabilities and computer vision systems. Since launching their R1 drone in 2018, Skydio has served over 1,200 enterprise customers including every branch of the U.S. military.

Skydio became the first U.S. drone company to reach a $1 billion valuation, generating over $100 million in annual revenue in 2023, with 30% coming from software solutions. The company has a local office in Israel and sells its drones to the Israeli military. The Israeli company DefenSync is its authorized partner in Israel.

Based on a report by Theia Chatelle, the Yale Police Department (YPD) utilized Skydio drones as part of their surveillance program targeting pro-Palestine student protesters. 

According to a Wired investigation, a Skydio X10 drone equipped with multiple high-resolution cameras, thermal imaging, powerful zoom capabilities, and onboard AI was detected monitoring pro-Palestine protesters at the Democratic National Convention in Chicago, with the same drone later being spotted above the Israeli consulate during subsequent protests.

In October 2025, The Washington Post revealed that Skydio provided the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) remote-controlled drones, reportedly used to film protesters and monitor public demonstrations.

In April 2026, Skydio committed $3.5 billion over five years to expand U.S. manufacturing, R&D, and supply chains, including a new "SkyForge" facility five times the size of its current space.

properties.name: Skynet
properties.description:
Skynet (天网系统), China's massive surveillance infrastructure, represents one of the world's most extensive monitoring networks. Initially launched in 2005, the system has expanded dramatically from its original 20 million cameras to encompass approximately 170 million cameras by 2018, with plans to install an additional 400 million units across the country. 

The system features real-time monitoring capabilities, advanced AI-powered tracking systems, facial recognition technology, and a vast network of cameras to monitor public spaces and track individuals throughout China, as well as integration with other surveillance technologies. The central government oversees its operation through various agencies, including the Ministry of Public Security.

The Skynet cameras have been strategically positioned across multiple sensitive locations, with installations found outside mosques in Xinjiang, temples in Tibet, and the residences of dissidents.

properties.description:
Skypearl Ltd, a discreet Israeli start-up co-founded by Sergey Vichik, a former Google X engineer, and Ori Gonen, a former Israeli military officer, is a developer of stratospheric Intelligence and surveillance platforms. Their products include spy balloons for intelligence operations. 

These semi-autonomous balloons, part of the classified Tzafon Aerostat programme, were deployed since 2023 over Gaza. Skypearl has minimal public presence, with its headquarters registered in Herzliya and no official website or trade show appearances.

properties.name: Smart Communications
properties.description:
Smart Communications, a Florida-based company, provides surveillance and communication tools to over 150 prisons and jails across more than 25 U.S. states. Its MailGuard product digitizes postal mail sent to incarcerated individuals by scanning letters at remote facilities and uploading them as PDFs for inmates to view on tablets. 

The company also offers a surveillance system called Smart Tracker, which monitors not only the communications of incarcerated individuals but also those of the public who correspond with them. This system collects a wide range of data, including home addresses, IP addresses, email addresses, GPS locations, device information, and any linked accounts. By requiring users to create accounts through its "Smart Jail Mail" portal, the company ties this data to specific individuals, creating a detailed profile of those who communicate with prisoners. They also provide a searchable database of all messages sent and received by prisoners, along with identifying information about senders.

properties.name: SN Technologies
properties.description:
SN Technologies is the developer of the AEGIS platform, which combines facial recognition, video analytics and weapons detection. It analyzes CCTV feeds, compares faces against watchlists and generates real time alerts for flagged people or detected objects. The technology was deployed in Lockport, New York schools. The system used hundreds of cameras for facial and object recognition, and was configured to alert personnel and police agencies when individuals on a watchlist specific objects were detected.

The AEGIS platform was criticized over accuracy, racial bias, privacy and false positives. Documents reviewed by EPIC and reporting by VICE found that the technology had significant problems identifying Black faces and sometimes misidentified objects as guns.

An independent audit reviewed by the NYCLU found substantially higher racial disparities in misidentification than the company had disclosed: Black men were reportedly misidentified four times as often as white men, while Black women were misidentified 16 times as often. 

A consultant working with SN Technologies told Buffalo Toronto Public Media that AEGIS was being used by European law enforcement agencies, specifically Scotland Yard, INTERPOL and the French Ministry of Defense.

properties.name: SNA International
properties.description:
SNA International is a forensic science and biometrics contractor that provides DNA analysis, laboratory services, and rapid DNA identification technologies to government agencies. In 2025, the company was awarded an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) contract worth up to $28 million to implement rapid DNA testing for ICE's Enforcement and Removal Operations, enabling ICE to build and analyze large volumes of sensitive biometric and genetic data. 

The program is intended to verify biological relationships among individuals encountered during immigration enforcement, with ICE stating the technology is used to "identify fraudulent familial relationship claims." 

Human rights organizations have warned that this facilitates family separations, expands government genetic surveillance of migrants, and raises significant privacy concerns about the collection, retention, and future use of genetic information.

properties.name: Snaptrends
properties.kinds: Social Media Monitoring; Data Broker; Student Monitoring
properties.providing to: United States; Bangladesh; Saudi Arabia; Hong Kong; United Arab Emirates
properties.description:
Snaptrends was a social media monitoring and surveillance platform that developed ways to analyze geotagged social media posts and conversations in real time. The platform was marketed to law enforcement agencies, schools, and other organizations, enabling users to track keywords, hashtags, and geographic areas of interest. 

Law enforcement agencies across the United States utilized Snaptrends to track targets and monitor public events. For example, the software was reportedly used to increase arrest rates during specific operations. Snaptrends was also used to monitor students' social media activity, often in collaboration with schools. 

The company promoted social media analytics tools to authorities in Azerbaijan, Bahrain, Malaysia, Turkey, and other countries known to suppress online speech, according to confidential company documents and interviews with current and former employees. Beginning in 2013, Snaptrends pursued business in Saudi Arabia, entering a $500,000 agreement with a company linked to the royal family to sell its technology. The company also engaged with the Saudi Ministry of Interior and intelligence agencies. It has also done business with the United Arab Emirates.

In 2014, Brandon Burris, Snaptrends co-founder and chief technology officer at the time, flew to Hong Kong as part of a $300,000 deal with a local holding company Faith Concord. According to corporate filings in China, Faith Concord owns BaoLiDa, which markets its ability to monitor citizens’ activities on the internet to the Chinese government.

Snaptrends faced criticism for targeting activists or disproportionately affecting marginalized communities. These concerns led platforms like Twitter to sever ties with Snaptrends, cutting off access to their data in 2016. Snaptrends ceased operations later that year, laying off its staff and shutting down quietly.

properties.name: SocioSpyder
properties.description:
SocioSpyder is a software tool developed by Allied Associates International (A2I), designed to monitor and analyze social media activity. It allows law enforcement and intelligence agencies to collect, store, and analyze posts, tweets, videos, and chats from platforms like Facebook, Twitter, and YouTube. The tool can autonomously or on-demand compile this data into a searchable and graphable database. It also provides advanced features such as mapping user-to-user relationships and visualizing data to help analysts better understand social media interactions.

The FBI and the U.S. Marshals Service have used SocioSpyder for various intelligence operations. According to Motherboard, between August 2014 and September 2015, the FBI spent approximately $78,000 on the software and related licenses, while the U.S. Marshals Service spent around $22,500.

Allied Associates International was acquired by Redhorse in October, 2023.

ShotSpotter, which retained its name as a product after the rebrand, relies on a network of acoustic sensors that monitor urban environments, effectively turning public spaces into zones of constant surveillance. In addition to police departments, SoundThinking also has contracts with the U.S. Department of Defense in the military market and also maintains a partnership with Israeli weapons manufacturer Airobotics.

Spectra Group is a New Zealand technology company whose surveillance products have been supplied to law enforcement and intelligence agencies. In Colombia, Spectra Group’s Laguna IMSI catcher was supplied through Colombian company Maicrotel Ltda. to the Colombian Police Intelligence Directorate (DIPOL) in September 2005, in a contract worth approximately US$474,000.

properties.description:
Speech Technology Center (STC,) also known as SpeechPro, is a Russian company that develops speech recognition, facial recognition and voice biometrics. It has its origins linked to a secretive Soviet technologies unit that operated under the KGB. According to Wired, the company's roots can be traced back to the Sharashka Marfino, a special prison for engineers and scientists during the Stalin era. In this facility, individuals plucked from various labor camps were coerced into developing technologies, including voice identification systems used for monitoring calls to foreign embassies in Moscow. According to its website, it worked with Saudi's Ministry of Interior to install an audio forensic lab in the Kingdom. 

In 2019, Sberbank, the state-controlled financial powerhouse, finalized the acquisition of a 51% stake in STC. Additionally, Digital Horizon, a venture capital and business incubator firm with offices in Moscow and Tel Aviv, also secured a stake in STC.

According to the BIRN (Balkan Investigative Reporting Network) investigation into surveillance systems in Serbia, STC's voice recognition software was procured by the Serbian Ministry of Internal Affairs (MUP). Serbian intermediary companies, notably AIGO and IntellSec, facilitated the supply to Serbian state institutions.

It can process and analyze digitized records, including data from CCTV feeds, images, and audio inputs. 

Trinetra 2.0, launched in collaboration with the Uttar Pradesh Police, incorporates Crime GPT to enhance policing capabilities, to provide real-time AI-assisted insights for intelligence operations. Staqu's technology is also deployed in prisons.

properties.name: T3K-Forensics
properties.description:
T3K-Forensics is an Austrian digital forensics company that provides automated analysis of data extracted from mobile phones and other digital devices. Its Law Enforcement Analytics Platform (LEAP) ingests data from various mobile extraction tools, including Cellebrite, MSAB, Oxygen Forensics and Grayshift, and uses AI and machine learning to identify information. T3K has marketed its technology to law enforcement, border control and immigration authorities.

properties.name: Tamoco
properties.funders: Rianta Capital; First Eastern
properties.description:
Tamoco is a data tracking startup leveraging a network of 1.1 billion proximity sensors to track the locations of approximately 100 million smartphone users. By partnering with apps that struggle to monetize, such as mobile games, offline maps, and deals apps, Tamoco integrates its tracking capabilities into these platforms. When users install these apps and accept the terms, their location data becomes part of Tamoco's network. Tamoco utilizes a combination of Wi-Fi signals, Bluetooth beacons, GPS, QR codes, and metadata (like device type, battery level, and dwell time) to track users. This data is then sold to third parties.

In 2023, Tamoco underwent an asset acquisition by PassBy, a company that also develops location-based technology.

properties.name: Team Cymru
properties.funders: Audax Private Equity
properties.description:
Team Cymru is a cybersecurity company founded headquartered in Florida that has developed significant data monitoring and threat intelligence capabilities. One of the company's platforms, Augury, bundles massive amounts of data purchased from the private sector and makes it available to government and corporate customers as a paid service. The tool claims to cover over 90% of the world's internet traffic, with multiple branches of the U.S. military collectively spending at least $3.5 million to access it. The platform provides access to sensitive data including email information, browsing history, and internet cookies. According to a U.S government procurement record reviewed by Motherboard, the data collection includes information from over 550 collection points worldwide, processing over 100 billion new records daily.

A particularly controversial aspect emerged when a whistleblower contacted Senator Ron Wyden's office regarding the Naval Criminal Investigative Service's (NCIS) alleged warrantless use of this data. While Team Cymru maintains that their platform cannot be used to target specific individuals or show patterns of life, the procurement records reveal access to detailed information including packet capture data (PCAP), web browser activity, and netflow data. The company obtains netflow data through partnerships with ISPs, who receive threat intelligence in return, though it's noted that ISP users are likely unaware their data is being shared and subsequently sold.

properties.description:
Telesoft Technologies is a telecommunications and network security company whose earlier products included lawful interception and mass monitoring systems supplied to law enforcement and intelligence agencies. Its HINTON range, documented in the WikiLeaks Spy Files, included passive probes capable of intercepting voice, SMS, cellular data and location information from fixed and mobile networks.

properties.name: Tendy Three
properties.description:
Tendy Three Investments (TTI) operates a public space CCTV surveillance system in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe, as part of a contract with the Bulawayo City Council. The system consists of street cameras installed across the city's Central Business District to monitor activity in public areas. properties.name: TheOneSpy
properties.description:
TheOneSpy is a remote monitoring application that markets itself for parental control and employee monitoring, but security researchers categorize it as "stalkerware" or a covert surveillance tool. It can track location, read SMS messages and call logs, monitor social media and emails, capture screenshots, record the screen, log keystrokes, and remotely activate a device's microphone and cameras.

A March 2025 study by University College London (UCL) examined TheOneSpy alongside other "sideloaded" or "unofficial" parental control apps and flagged serious privacy and safety concerns.

Because these apps are designed to operate covertly, they instruct users to disable Google Play Protect (Android's built-in malware defense) so the app won't be flagged and removed. TheOneSpy was among a minority of tested apps that Google Play Protect did not flag as harmful, meaning that even when Android's built-in defense is left active, it fails to warn the device owner, making the covert surveillance harder to detect.
properties.sources: Surveillance Disguised as Protection: A Comparative Analysis of Sideloaded and In-Store Parental Control Apps (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2504.16087); When 'Grandma-Proof' Android Spyware Is Good Enough For International Espionage (https://www.forbes.com/sites/thomasbrewster/2018/05/15/apple-iphone-spouseware-used-in-pakistan-government-attacks/)

properties.description:
Thomson Reuters, a major information and data provider, has signed at least three contracts with ICE totaling over $46 million specifically for surveillance services, including their CLEAR platform. The database contains over 400 million utility records, including names, addresses, and service details from utility companies, as well as employment, housing, and credit information. This data includes details sourced from Equifax and is updated daily and provides law enforcement with tools to locate individuals.

Thomson Reuters also helps power an app called Mobile Companion, built alongside Motorola Solutions, that lets ICE officers instantly scan a license plate in the field and add it to a database of billions of records showing where that vehicle has been spotted across the country. That vehicle data can then be combined with other personal information such as driver license data, credit header data, marriage records, vehicle ownership, and voter registrations. The app is also capable of predicting where a car may travel in the future and can collect face scans for facial recognition to help identify vehicle owners. The tool is designed for real-time use by ICE officials in the field, functioning similarly to the agency's existing facial recognition apps but focused on gathering information about vehicles.

properties.description:
TigerSwan is a global firm founded in 2008 by James Reese, a retired U.S. Army lieutenant colonel and former Delta Force commander. The company led the surveillance operations and infiltration of the Dakota Access Pipeline (DAPL) protests at Standing Rock. Hired by Energy Transfer, the company behind the pipeline, TigerSwan used a range of methods to monitor and disrupt the Indigenous-led resistance movement. These tactics included the use of undercover operatives, aerial surveillance, social media monitoring, and the creation of detailed dossiers on activists. The firm also collaborated with law enforcement, sharing intelligence and supporting legal actions against protestors.

Following its involvement at Standing Rock, TigerSwan sought to profit from its surveillance tactics by marketing its "counterinsurgency" playbook to other energy companies. The firm created detailed marketing materials and presentations, pitching its strategies to corporations like ConocoPhillips and Dominion Energy, which were involved in other contentious oil and gas projects.

properties.description:
Toka is an Israeli company launched in 2018 as a "one-stop hacking shop for governments," developing tools that give law enforcement, intelligence, and military clients the ability to remotely hack into any internet-connected device, beyond smartphones, specifically targeting Internet of Things (IoT) devices like Amazon Echos, Google Nest products, connected fridges, thermostats, alarms, and security cameras.

The company was co-founded by former Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Barak, retired IDF Brigadier General Yaron Rosen (former Chief of the IDF's cyber staff and lead architect of all IDF cyber activities, including those of Unit 8200), Alon Kantor (former VP of Business Development at Check Point Software, a firm founded by Unit 8200 veterans), and Kfir Waldman (former CEO of Go Arc and former Director of Engineering at Cisco).

As of December 2024, the company has raised $37.5 million and works exclusively with governments, including U.S. agencies, militaries, and law enforcement. Toka is expanding its U.S. operations, hiring roles like a "Client Director USA" to grow its business with the Department of Defense and national security agencies. The company recruited Mike Stahala, a former FBI attaché in Ankara, Turkey, for its Washington, D.C. office.

Countries known to have engaged Toka include Nigeria, Ghana, Moldova, and Chile. Specifically, they are confirmed as recipients of Toka's defensive "Cyber Designers" cybersecurity advisory services, funded through the World Bank and Inter-American Development Bank. Israeli media has reported these development bank partnerships were planned by a Netanyahu-era inter-ministerial committee aimed at advancing Israel's political interests in the developing world.

properties.description: ToTok was a messaging app that gained popularity in the UAE and other countries before it was removed from app stores in late 2019 over allegations that it was a spyware tool used by the UAE government to monitor its users. properties.description:
Travizory is a Swiss company that develops advanced border and surveillance technology. Its primary product, the API-PNR Targeting System, utilizes real-time traveler data, including Advance Passenger Information (API) and Passenger Name Records (PNR), to assess "risks" and identify individuals of interest before they cross borders. The system integrates AI-powered profiling and automated alerts for use by border officials, connecting governments with transport operators, and uses its AI for decision-making on which passengers to prevent from entering a country.

Currently operational in Kenya and the Seychelles, Travizory is also in discussions to expand its system to 20 other African countries.

properties.description:
Utimaco is a cybersecurity and compliance solutions provider that develops surveillance technology that supports data interception and retention. Their key product in this area is the Lawful Interception Management System (LIMS), which is used by law enforcement agencies to monitor and intercept communications data within a network. This system facilitates the interception of voice, data, and internet traffic, ensuring that the intercepted information can be securely transferred to law enforcement monitoring facilities.

According to the European Center for Constitutional and Human Rights (ECCHR), Utimaco was involved in supporting a centralized surveillance system operated by Syrian Telecom, even as late as 2011 when protests against Assad's regime began. Syrian Telecom, which is closely linked to the government and reportedly controlled by Syrian intelligence, closely collaborated with Utimaco on this project. Utimaco partnered with the Italian company Area SpA and the French firm Qosmos SA for this work. 

Utimaco was implicated in Iran's surveillance activities through its involvement in providing technology used for monitoring communications. properties.name: Valid
properties.description:
Valid is a Brazilian identity and technology company that provides facial and fingerprint biometrics, identity verification, and liveness detection, and markets these capabilities to government and law enforcement customers. Its current platform can perform automated facial matching against reference databases.

Valid has also developed facial recognition applications for law enforcement agencies. In 2025, the company described systems used by Brazilian police to identify targeted individuals in crowds, including a facial recognition deployment at a São João festival in São Luís, Maranhão, where Valid supported technology generated alerts by matching faces against databases of people.

In Paraná, Valid was contracted by the state owned IT company Celepar in 2022 to provide a system for identifying students through facial biometric recognition. The system was designed to process the biometric data of up to one million children per month, with images stored on government servers. Valid partnered with Slovak facial recognition company Innovatrics for this purpose.

In 2026, Brazil’s National Data Protection Authority (ANPD) ordered Paraná to halt the collection of children’s and adolescents’ biometric data for facial recognition attendance, citing inadequate legal basis, security and governance safeguards.

U.S.-Israeli company Verint provides eavesdropping equipment, including "monitoring centers" that allow for the interception, monitoring, and analysis of both targeted and mass communications across various networks. These systems are integrated into a country's communication infrastructure and are capable of intercepting phone calls and emails from millions of citizens, storing the data for analysis. Verint's technology is employed in over 75 countries and can be used for nationwide mass interception, voice identification, and data mining to build detailed profiles of individuals.

Verint sold their technology to repressive regimes worldwide, including in Azerbaijan, Indonesia, South Sudan, Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan. The technology sold to Azerbaijan was reportedly used to identify the sexual orientations of individuals through social media, leading to the targeting and arrest of LGBTQ+ individuals. In the Gulf region, Verint products have been used to gather data from social networks, contributing to the repression of dissidents for their online activities. Additionally, in Indonesia, Verint's technology has been employed to compile databases of LGBTQ+ rights activists and monitor religious minorities. The company has also sold its SS7-based tracking tool SkyLock to a government client in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

Verint has been linked to surveillance operations in South Sudan, where it provided communications interception equipment and support services to the government. This arrangement required the telecommunications company Vivacell to pay Verint over $762,000 to facilitate the interception of citizens' communications, as reported by Amnesty International. 

In 2025, the company agreed to be acquired by private equity firm Thoma Bravo in a deal valued at approximately $2 billion.

Veritone is an enterprise AI company that provides surveillance and investigative tools to law enforcement and government agencies. Its primary product, Veritone Track, is a video forensics platform that enables users to identify and track individuals and vehicles across large amounts of video footage, including body cameras, CCTV, drones, and social media feeds.

A significant upgrade to Veritone Track was announced in October 2024, expanding its capabilities to include AI-assisted vehicle tracking at scale. This update allows investigators to trace vehicles of interest across multiple video sources. The platform's AI engine supposedly analyzes video footage to identify vehicles by their visual features. Its customers include the U.S Department of Homeland Security. 

Microsoft Azure provides Veritone with cloud computing resources to support its AI-powered surveillance platforms.

properties.description:
VIDIZMO is a video intelligence and surveillance technology company that markets AI-powered tools to law enforcement and other organizations. According to a September 2026 investigation by 404 Media, the company has promoted integrating data from Flock’s automated license plate reader cameras with VIDIZMO’s own platforms.

VIDIZMO also markets facial recognition, license plate readers and video analysis capabilities that can identify people from watchlists, trigger alerts and recordings when enrolled individuals appear on camera, and classify or filter people by estimated age, gender, and race. 404 Media reported that VIDIZMO has begun offering facial recognition technology to police since early 2026.

The company’s CEO, Nadeem Khan, told 404 Media that VIDIZMO "would love to do the integration" with Flock and described facial recognition as an inevitable direction for surveillance technology. 

VIDIZMO’s government and law-enforcement clients include the Baltimore Police Department, Adams County Sheriff’s Office, DuPage County Sheriff’s Office, Georgia Attorney General’s Office, California Department of Motor Vehicles, Dallas County, Missouri Department of Revenue, the U.S. Department of State, and the U.S. Air Force, according to the company’s own customer and case study materials.

properties.description:
Viisights develops behavioral video analytics powered by artificial intelligence. One of their products, Wise, is designed to analyze real-time video feeds to detect and interpret human behaviors. Viisights has been reportedly used in monitoring refugees in Greece as part of the EU-funded Centaur surveillance system. This system, which includes tools from other Israeli companies, has been criticized for creating "prison-like" conditions for refugees. The refugee camps, such as the one on the island of Samos, have been described as "testing grounds" for surveillance technologies later deployed elsewhere in Europe.

Viisights' behavioral video analytics are also used by Israel's Ministry of Public Security and in smart city initiatives, such as in the city of Eilat, to detect and analyze events in real-time.

The company's Wise platform has been integrated with Cognyte's Symphia solutions, to improve the capabilities of both systems for behavioral video recognition. Cognyte is a prominent Israeli vendor of surveillance products.

properties.description: WeChat, known as Weixin in China, is a multifunctional messaging app developed by Tencent.
